title: Nexgen OS GeoJSON export, version 1
description: The document `exportGeoJson()` of `@nexgen-os/core` writes: a participant, or a project and every participant taking part in it, as one RFC 7946 FeatureCollection — the places and the figures computed on them together, so that a study can be shown to the people it concerns. With `open: true` it is the document meant for the public (a citizens' portal, a consultation, an open-data catalogue, a publication): no street line, no serial number, no metadata, nothing from a source that may not be passed on. `importGeoJsonParticipants()` reads the participants of such a document back. A property is added to this schema in the same change that adds it to the export; a property renamed or removed is a version 2.

bbox.description: West, south, east, north — with the lowest and highest heights when the positions carry one: around every position of the collection (RFC 7946 §5).

id.description: The object's identifier in Nexgen OS.

geometry.description: WGS 84 longitude, latitude and, when known, height in metres, seven decimals; outer rings counter-clockwise, holes clockwise (RFC 7946 §3.1.6). Null for a device (a device is not placed) and for an object described without a shape.

properties.description: The columns of the object, named as the model names them, then what is attached to it. A property a kind of object does not have is absent, and a property an open export never carries is absent from it.

kind.description: Which object of the model the feature is: the project (first, when a project is exported), a participant, and — with the `building` module — its ground (`site`), its buildings and their surfaces; then the devices.

attributes.description: The attributes of the object holding at the export's moment (`nexgen_os.at`), as `attributes_of()` reads them: attribute type → value. An open export leaves out those a source that may not be passed on gave.

identifiers.description: The identifiers the object is known by elsewhere (a register, a meter point, a building identifier), scheme by scheme, holding at the export's moment. An open export leaves out those a source that may not be passed on gave.

calculations.description: The figures the installed modules computed on the object, each as its module keeps it (`solar.estimates`, `community.settlements`…), oldest first. The export computes nothing; empty when the export was asked without them. An open export keeps them: a study shown to the public is its figures beside its places.

project_kind.description: project: its kind, a code of `project_kinds`.

country.description: project, participant: the country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. A participant is a feature only when it has one.

status.description: project, participant, building, device: its status, as the model keeps it.

project_id.description: participant: the project it takes part in.

segment.description: participant: its segment, a code of `segments`.

address_line1.description: participant: the street line of its address. Never in an open export.

address_line2.description: participant: the second street line of its address. Never in an open export.

postal_code.description: participant: the postal code of its address.

city.description: participant: the city of its address.

region.description: participant: the region of its address.

municipality.description: participant: the code of its municipality, in the scheme of its country.

time_zone.description: participant: its IANA time zone, which its daily readings follow.

location_precision.description: participant: how precisely its geometry places it (a building, an address, a postal code, a municipality…).

location_source_code.description: participant: the source that placed it, a code of `nexgen_os.sources`. An open export keeps the address of a participant placed by a source that may not be passed on, and drops its geometry.

participant_id.description: site, building, surface, device: the participant it belongs to.

site_id.description: building, surface: the ground it stands on.

building_id.description: surface: the building it is a face of; null for a ground area.

use.description: site, building: what it is used for.

area_m2.description: site, surface: its area in square metres.

elevation_m.description: building: the height of its ground above sea level, in metres.

height_m.description: building: its height above its ground, in metres.

year_built.description: building: the year it was built.

floor_area_m2.description: building: its floor area, in square metres.

energy_label.description: building: its energy label, as its country writes it.

surface_kind.description: surface: a roof face, a facade, a ground area…

azimuth_deg.description: surface: the direction it faces, in degrees clockwise from true north.

tilt_deg.description: surface: its tilt from the horizontal, in degrees.

u_value.description: surface: its thermal transmittance, in W/(m²·K).

is_external.description: surface: whether it faces the outside.

global_id.description: site, building, surface: its identifier in the source it was read from (an IFC GlobalId, an OpenStreetMap way…).

source_code.description: site, building, surface, device: the source that described it, a code of `nexgen_os.sources`. An open export withholds an object described by a source that may not be passed on, with everything on it.

metadata.description: site, building, surface: what its source said beyond the columns. Never in an open export.

device_type.description: device: its type, a code of `device_types`.

serial_number.description: device: its serial number. Never in an open export.

rated_power_kw.description: device: its rated power, in kW.

unit_count.description: device: how many units it counts (modules of an array, points of a charging station…).

installation_date.description: device: the day it was installed.

value.description: The identifier, as its scheme writes it.

module.description: The code of the module that keeps it.

table.description: The module's table it is kept in: `estimates`, `settlements`…

provenance.description: Where it comes from: the program and the version that computed it.

updated_at.description: When the module last wrote it, ISO 8601 in UTC.

results.description: The results, exactly as the module keeps them.

about.description: Foreign member: what the document is and what it owes. Nothing in it depends on the moment the export ran: the same database gives the same document.

schema_version.description: The version of the Nexgen OS schema the document was read from.

at.description: The moment attributes and identifiers were read at, ISO 8601 in UTC; null for the moment of the export.

open.description: Whether this is the open export, meant for the public.

sources.description: Every source a feature, an attribute or an identifier of the document came from, with its licence and its attribution, by code.

withheld.description: How many objects an open export left out because their source, or the source of the object they belong to, may not be passed on.

license.description: Its licence, an SPDX identifier when there is one.

attribution.description: The attribution it asks for, to show beside what it gave.
